subject: Pricing and commit tiers — request to match OpenAI rates
messages:
From: Evan Carter <evan.carter@acmeai.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmeai.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick question on pricing / match to OpenAI

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. AcmeAI is evaluating hosted inference providers to replace a portion of our OpenAI spend for customer-facing features. A few quick pricing questions before we loop procurement: 

- Can Redwood offer per-token usage pricing that is competitive with public OpenAI/Anthropic endpoints (we're benchmarking against OpenAI's completion price of $0.0004 / token)?
- What discounts do you offer for committed monthly spend tiers (e.g., $20k / $50k / $100k per month)?
- Do you have a formal price-match policy or a way to displace a public provider on contract? 

Primary goal is cost parity or better on unit economics while keeping the same level of throughput and latency for our product. Happy to do a short call with pricing/procurement if that helps.

Best,
Evan Carter
Head of Platform
AcmeAI

Hi Evan —

Great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front: yes, we can structure per-token pricing and commit tiers to be competitive with public providers, and we do have an evaluation process for price-matching / displacement requests. Below is a concise outline and an attached proposal PDF with sample pricing by tier.

Summary (high level):
- Usage model: per-token consumption for generations + embeddings. Token accounting mirrors OpenAI-style semantics (prompt + completion tokens).
- Commit tiers (example):
  * Tier A: $20k/mo commit — baseline discount ~18% off list
  * Tier B: $50k/mo commit — baseline discount ~26% off list
  * Tier C: $100k+/mo commit — baseline discount ~35% off list + reserved throughput
- Competitive match: we review the competitor price (public list or redacted invoice), verify feature parity (rate limits, latency SLOs, model family), and then propose a binding short-term match (typically 3–6 months) as part of a pilot + commit.
- Add-ons: Dedicated capacity, enhanced SLOs, and data residency are available as separate line items.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review the attached "ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Proposal.pdf" — sample numbers assume Gen-1 family models (quantized).
2) If you want a written match, please share the competitor pricing you want matched (screenshot/invoice) and the commit horizon AcmeAI would target.
3) We can set a 30-minute pricing review with our sales manager and legal to draft a short-term price-protection addendum.

I'll have Vivek join for technical quals during the call (KV-cache behavior, batching impact on token economics). Would Thu 26 Feb at 10:00 PT work?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:47:00 -0800

Evan —

Couple of technical clarifications that affect unit cost comparisons:

- Effective token cost depends on prompt engineering and reuse. Our platform's prefix/KV caching can reduce chargeable prompt tokens in many flows (we can quantify on your test set).
- Throughput/latency: if you're comparing endpoint rates, note that public endpoints sometimes throttle tail latency. For a price match we will need to confirm the throughput SLO to ensure like-for-like economics (CPU/GPU sizing affects $/token when you factor in concurrency).
- Model variants: public provider may be using a different model family; model-architecture parity matters for quality vs cost comparisons. We can run a micro-eval on a 2000-sample prompt set and include token consumption profiles.

I can prepare a 2-tab spreadsheet: (1) unit price + projected monthly spend, (2) test-set token counts and expected monthly token volume. Will aim to have this ready by Wed EOD.

— Vivek
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa/Vivek —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement asked for the following so they can evaluate in parallel: 

1) A written price-match commitment vs. OpenAI public completion price: OpenAI public list shows $0.0004 / token for the model family we're using. We're requesting a firm written parity for the first 6 months if we commit to $50k/month.

2) Confirmation of no extra per-request surcharges (we need a single blended $/token rate, not hidden infra fees).

3) A proposed SLA for latency and a fallback plan if Redwood needs to throttle (we have regulatory customers and can't have silent degradations).

If you can supply the price-match letter and the simple spreadsheet Vivek mentioned, we can route through procurement and legal next week. If you prefer, I'll sign a short pilot DocuSign with the $50k/mo commit and 6-month term contingent on receiving the match in writing.

Best,
Evan

Team — quick internal note to align before we send anything official to AcmeAI: 

- We can offer a binding price-protection addendum that matches a public OpenAI rate for up to 6 months on the condition of a $50k/mo minimum committed spend. This should be explicit about model family (Gen-1 quantized assumption) and exclude dedicated capacity line items.
- For procurement: agree to a single blended $/token rate (no infra surcharges) for the duration of the addendum. Include language for a 30-day notice if we need to change that rate after the 6-month window; otherwise fixed.
- SLA: propose a 99.9% uptime for hosted API and a latency SLO for P95; include automatic fallback routing to a compatible model variant in case of capacity constraints (documented).
- Commercial counter: offer 30% off list (internal baseline) at $50k/mo commit for the 6-month pilot; if Acme moves to $100k+/mo within 90 days, trigger an additional 5% rebate applied retroactively.

Marissa — please pull together a short price-match letter + the Vivek spreadsheet and route through legal (I created a HubSpot note under the deal). Once legal gives thumbs-up, send DocuSign to Evan.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
